item.title: [vogue.com] The Bride Wore a Pearlescent, Ocean-Inspired Wardrobe for Her Harbour Island Wedding
item.dc:creator: Shelby Wax

item.content:encoded:
A game of truth or dare led high school best friends Bella Pepin and Cameron Kenny to realize they should be something more. “But my junior year and his senior year, everything changed,” Bella recalls. The two were dared to kiss each other at a Halloween party, and they automatically felt a spark. “We started dating pretty much immediately and dated through the rest of high school and throughout college with a few on-and-offs,” says Bella. After college, the two Florida natives drifted apart and didn’t see each other for five years. A chance meeting at a bar out in Montauk changed their fate. “We were too nervous to say hi to each other for over an hour or so,” she shares. “Eventually, we briefly chatted, but nothing came of that night!” Back in NYC, Bella decided to be forward and ask Cameron to grab coffee. “We ended up walking six miles in circles on the West Side Highway, catching up on the last five years of life. It felt like we picked back up right where we left off,” she shares. “We were so young when we first dated, so the time apart really allowed us to grow up and learn ourselves. Getting back together this time, we both knew it was for good.”
Two years later, the couple moved in together in Dallas with a golden retriever named Goose and a cat named Rigatoni. The following spring, Cameron proposed to Bella on his 31st birthday while they were on a trip together on Harbour Island, a place he has traveled to with his family for years. “He waited until the second night of the trip to propose—which really threw me off,” says Bella. The two were walking on the beach to dinner at sunset when Cameron popped the question as a hidden photographer captured the moment. The two continued the night with celebrations at dinner and calls with their families to tell them the news. “That same weekend, Cameron wasted no time and surprised me with a tour of The Other Side—our wedding venue,” says Bella. “It was full speed ahead!”
The two decided to have their friends and family join them for their Bahamas destination wedding on April 11, 2026. “There is something really special about it,” Bella says of Harbour Island. “We love the relaxed yet refined vibe, the food, the design, and the people… We never considered a wedding anywhere else.” Bella, who works as an interior designer, partnered up with their wedding planner Sophia Goff to execute their vision. “Sophia is a creative genius, and we immediately clicked,” she says. “Knowing how much I cared, she let me into the weeds with her—reviewing fabric samples and tabletop tailoring details and so much more. I’m so grateful she brought me behind the scenes.” The groom gives the two all the credit. Cameron adds, “I only helped manage the band and requested no lines at any bars!”
The vision for the weekend was to have a unique, elevated design perspective, without it feeling too serious. “Island-y, but not beach-y,” explains Bella. “All of our events were outdoors—with the exception of a rehearsal dinner pivot due to rain—so we wanted the designs to mimic natural Caribbean elements, sticking to a color and material palette seen in the surrounding tropical landscape.” The bride also put particular care into the invitations and paper goods throughout the weekend, hiring calligrapher Emily Snyder to create playful illustrations for the designs. The bride adds, “The kissing fish she doodled are everything to me!”
This design ethos also translated into Bella’s style choices for the weekend. “I wanted my wardrobe to feel classic, yet fun with loads of island influence,” she says. “The location lent itself to lots of texture and fun accessorizing—raffia fringe, sheer materials, floral appliqués, pearls, shells, and fish!” The bride credits her friend, stylist Madison Childs Lee, as a major help in curating her weekend ensembles. “She innately has a really cool eye, is a master at sourcing unique pieces, and helped me pull together the final touches on each look,” Bella shares.
The bride kicked off the weekend in a Danielle Frankel gown with hand-painted appliqués and baroque pearl tendrils for the rehearsal dinner. “I felt like a mermaid that just came from the sea,” she reminisces. For the beach day, Bella donned a sheer, lacework dress from Matin’s fall collection. She adds, “I think I saw a runway photo of it on their Instagram, and knew I needed it for the weekend!” The welcome party look by Holli Studio was one of the bride’s favorites. “The butter leather top and skirt with raffia fringe didn’t feel overly bridal and were so fun and flirty to wear,” she says. “I can't wait to rewear it.” Bella paired the set with a silver and pearl shell necklace her mom bought on her honeymoon in St. Croix in the ’80s. “Immediate prized possession status,” she adds.
For her trip down the aisle, the bride wore Danielle Frankel’s Arlo gown, a high-neck silk wool dress with pearl-like sheen, a low back, and raw chiffon trim. “I knew I wanted to be a Danielle Frankel bride, so much so that I didn’t try on any other bridal lines,” she says. “I worked with the team at the NYC studio on custom additions, and we ended up adding more of the raw chiffon material around the bust and down the waist. I love the added texture and airiness it gave the look.” She paired the look with a custom shell pouch from the brand by Sloan and custom diamond and pearl earrings by her friend Lili George made to mimic an Art Deco pair she once saw at an estate sale. “They added a touch of old-world to the look and I’ll cherish them forever,” Bella gushes.
Cameron kept his wedding weekend looks classic in custom suiting by P Johnson and Sid Mashburn. Tones of the looks were in blues, greens, and neutrals to mirror the design palette. “For the wedding day, he wanted to wear an ivory dinner jacket as a nod to what he wore when he took me to his senior prom,” shares Bella. “He wore cufflinks engraved with our initials gifted by me on wedding day, and black raffia loafers to give the look a bit more of an island feel.” She adds, “He looked so handsome.”
The weekend kicked off with a rehearsal dinner filled with speeches and classic Bahamian dishes served family style. “The interior design style of Pink Sands Hotel feels very British West Indies, so we leaned in,” shares the bride. “We had to move the dinner from their garden into the restaurant at the last minute due to rain, but I honestly think being inside the hotel gave more context to our design.” The night ended at a dive bar named Gusty’s complete with a disco ball and never-ending early-2000s hits. “We stayed out later than planned, but it was so much fun,” says Bella.
The following day, guests hit the beach at Ms. V’s and enjoyed painkillers, local beer, and fish sandwiches. “It was so fun to be hanging on the beach, sunning and swimming with all of our people in a more casual setting before the wedding events kicked off,” shares the bride. That night, the welcome party at Coral Sands Hotel’s Beach Bar was a “full-on shell explosion.” Custom coasters, aprons, menus, and mosaics all featured shell motifs. “We wanted to be super playful to go with the loud and punchy decor of the hotel,” Bella says.
The bride and groom spurred tradition and saw each other the morning of the wedding for a sunrise swim in the ocean. “It was the highlight of the weekend for me,” shares Bella. “Break the rules! See each other before the wedding!” As the ceremony approached, windy weather led to some last-minute changes. “I started with my hair styled down and 10 minutes before walking down the aisle, Alejandra threw it up into a bun,” says the bride. “We also ended up flipping the ceremony seating so guests were facing away from the ocean to avoid wind feedback on the mic. You can only plan for so much!”
The couple legally tied the knot in their hometown in Florida five months earlier, which helped shed some of the nerves around the ceremony. “I think we both felt more excited than nervous,” says the bride. “Cameron’s uncle Davis officiated, and we recited our own personal vows, which were very teary. How can you put a 15-year-long journey into two minutes?!” The newlyweds recessed to “Oh La La” by Faces and felt like they were in a movie. “We had a sweet moment to ourselves and cheersed with a spritz before joining the guests at cocktails on the lawn,” remembers Bella.
The cocktail and reception spaces were filled with native plants and overgrown florals. “The Other Side has a very weathered and wild vibe to it, and Sophia and I kept coming back to this idea of a deserted island,” says Bella. “But, of course, [we had] a really chic dressed-up dinner with silk taffeta table linens for a bit of unexpected fancy. It was black tie after all.”
Before dinner, the couple shared their first dance to “Cruisin’” by Smokey Robinson. “My mom raised my sisters and I on soul and Motown, and I’ve always loved this song. But now it holds a bigger meaning for us,” says the bride. Cameron danced to “In My Life” by The Beatles with his mother, and Bella’s father gave a speech with a Phil Collins-inspired intro. “It was nothing short of iconic, and got the crowd on their feet,” she shares.
The bride changed into a TWP strapless dress and shell necklace as the dancing really kicked off. The band played a curated setlist that kept the dance floor packed all night. Cameron notes, “It was electric!” The night transitioned to the after-party complete with a DJ and live saxophone player. “The groomsmen had my dad on their shoulders at one point, and even my 11-year-old sister stayed ‘til the early morning hours,” says Bella. “We never wanted it to end!”
Reflecting on the weekend, the bride says, “We’re just so happy, and everything felt so authentically us: the design, place, the music, our people, all of it.” Adds the groom, “I wouldn’t change a thing! I wish we could do it all again.”

item.content:encoded:
Tom Parker’s widow Kelsey Parker found a second chance at love with boyfriend Will Lindsay while coping with grief.
Kelsey and Tom were married from 2018 until his death in March 2022 at age 33. The Wanted member died following his battle with brain cancer. Kelsey and Tom welcomed two children, Aurelia and Bodhi, in July 2019 and October 2020, respectively.
Years after Tom’s passing, Kelsey shared that she was dating again and revealed her new romance with Lindsay in September 2024. Four months later, Kelsey announced that she was pregnant with her and Lindsay’s first child.
“Tom and I always said we wanted four — but life had other plans,” she told The Mirror in January 2025. “So yes, this is amazing but also bittersweet. The joys of finding out I’m pregnant and moving forward with my life, while thinking, ‘My life could have been so different. I’ve felt every emotion under the sun.”
In June 2025, Kelsey announced the loss of their baby, sharing that he was “born sleeping.”
“Phoenix Parker-Lindsay, you will forever be loved,” she wrote via Instagram at the time.
Keep scrolling for a complete timeline of Kelsey and Lindsay’s relationship:
September 2024
Two years after Tom’s death, Kelsey made her Lindsay’s romance Instagram Official. The post included a photo of the couple hugging while Lindsay’s head turned away from the camera and was captioned with a single red heart emoji. After making their relationship official, Kelsey took to social media to thank fans for their kind words.
“I was really hesitant to share this part of my life, especially since many of you know me from my life with Tom and the horrific grief I’ve been dealing with after losing him,” she penned. “Opening up about my journey over the past couple of years has been incredibly healing, allowing me to connect with others who’ve gone through similar experiences and build a beautiful, supportive community.”
October 2024
During an October 2024 episode of Kelsey’s “Mum’s the Word” podcast with Georgia Jones, Kelsey shared that she and Lindsay “met authentically” and they had already introduced each other to their families.
“He just makes me really happy. And I think for me, I’ve been trying to find happiness for a little while now. I’m always going to have that guilt, I guess that’s part of the grief process.” she explained. “Having the guilt that I’m here and I’ve met someone but it will never take away the love I had for Tom. And with Will he would never try and take that away from me either.”
November 2024
While appearing on the British talk show Lorraine, Kelsey gave some more details about how she and Lindsay first connected.
“We met out with friends, he was out with a group of boys and I was out with a group of girls and we just had a connection,” she gushed. “I just wanted to meet someone authentic. I couldn’t have done [a] dating app, I was so scared and it was the judgment from people about moving on and meeting someone, but everyone’s so supportive.”
January 2025
Kelsey and Lindsay announced that they were expecting their first child together.
“I’m over the moon. This is something I’ve wanted for a long time,” Lindsay told The Mirror. “I couldn’t be happier and I know Kelsey is going to be an amazing mum, as she already is.”
April 2025
Lindsay and Kelsey took a family trip to Gran Canaria, Spain.
“Nothing beats a family holiday to Gran Canaria!!” Kelsey wrote via Instagram alongside a photo of the family of the group out to dinner. “These trips will always have a special place in our hearts, we always have the best time ☀️ Soaking up these moments before our family grows… 🤰🏼.”
June 2025
Kelsey announced that she and Lindsay lost their baby, whom they named Phoenix. The post included a poem written in honor of the late newborn, who was born stillborn.
“For Phoenix, Born Sleeping, Forever Loved,” the poem began. “The world grew quiet as you arrived / So loved, so longed for, yet not alive / Our precious boy, our angel light / Born with wings, took silent flight. We named you Phoenix, brave and bright / A soul of love, of warmth and light / Though we never heard you cry / You’ll live in hearts that won’t ask why. No breath you drew, no eyes to see / Still, you mean everything to me / You’ll journey with us, softly near / In every sigh, in every tear.”
May 2026
Kelsey announced her pregnancy with her and Lindsay’s rainbow baby nearly one year after Phoenix’s death.
“A year ago next month, we lost our beautiful baby boy, Phoenix 🤍,” she wrote via Instagram. “And somehow, through all the heartbreak, it feels like Tom and Phoenix have sent us another little gift from heaven our little rainbow baby ✨.”
September 2026
Kelsey and Lindsay welcomed daughter River, calling her “our little bit of hope.”

item.content:encoded:
Pedro Acosta is finally a MotoGP race winner, after he took an emotional first victory at the Austrian Grand Prix on KTM’s home turf.
The Spaniard had to wait 56 premier class starts before he could break his duck, something that seemed unfathomable when he made his debut at the start of the 2024 season.
Acosta was quick from the off at the Red Bull Ring, but he had to win the grand prix the hard way on Sunday.
A certain victory in the sprint was thrown away when he crashed with three laps to go, while he left his KTM team with more repair work to do on Sunday morning when he fell in warm-up.
But once he took the lead on lap nine of 28 in the main race, he never looked back, as he had the measure of Aprilia’s Jorge Martin.
It’s a win that closes a circle for the Acosta/KTM relationship, with the 22-year-old moving on to Ducati next season.
But could it get even better for both parties in the remaining races of 2026?
Though 72 points adrift in the standings, Marc Marquez firmly considers Acosta a title contender and has already branded him the favourite for the upcoming Japanese Grand Prix.
On the latest Crash MotoGP Podcast, Amy Reynolds is joined by Lewis Duncan and Peter McLaren to discuss the Austrian Grand Prix and whether or not Acosta can still fight for the 2026 title.
The team also discuss Acosta’s character and what to expect long-term when he goes up against Marc Marquez at Ducati in 2027.
Elsewhere, they discuss Jorge Martin’s strong weekend and his 12-point lead in the championship, asking if this is the Spaniard’s true return to form.
Ducati’s difficult weekend at the Red Bull Ring is analysed, as most of its riders were well off the pace, while Marc Marquez battled a brake issue in the grand prix.

item.content:encoded:
Some of the best romance movies ever made have tackled some difficult territory, examining the complicated topics of marriage and divorce alike. While many of the most satisfying endings seen in film have closed happily, some of the strongest dramatic entries have taken a harder look at emotions, chronicling the difficult dissolutions of relationships and marriages.
Movies about divorces are not always easy to watch. Many such stories delve into the complex emotional turmoil that the falling apart of a relationship can hold. Loaded with heartbreak and genuine pain, these stories provide deep points of connection that can help anyone going through such a struggle find ways to still feel human.
However, considering a marriage that ends in divorce to be a failure is such a limiting way of looking at the world.
Seeing the connections that blossom between two people, even if they do not last forever, is an important emotional factor in movies about humans and relationships. Not every love lasts forever, but this does not take away from the value that it has provided to a life.
Sometimes letting go of a relationship is worth celebrating, not just grieving. Many of these complex films examine the fallouts of those relationships in different and often surprising ways. Moving on is a part of life, and seeing how that works can fill these stories with sadness, joy, humor, and heartbreak all at once, making these films essential watches.
Divorce Italian Style
An unusual look at marriage and divorce, this fantastic 1961 comedy directed by Pietro Germi deeply questions a number of confusing social mores. In the film, Ferdinando, a poor Sicilian nobleman played by Marcello Mastroianni, falls in love with his sixteen-year-old cousin, Angela, and wishes to be with her.
However, Ferdinando is married, and divorce is illegal. However, considering the law's lax treatment of honor killings, he devises an absurd path to being with Angela: he will secretly find his wife a new lover, catch them in the act, and murder her. After serving a short prison sentence, he will be able to be with Angela.
This convoluted path highlights major issues with Italian law, and does so with great humor. A twisted and hilarious story, Divorce Italian Style is one of the more outsized and comedic looks at marriage and relationships on this list.
War Of The Roses
Danny DeVito has directed some fantastic films, and War of the Roses might be his best. This dark and funny 1989 comedy examines the dissolution of a marriage between Oliver and Barbara Rose, played by Michael Douglas and Kathleen Turner respectively. Rounding out the cast, DeVito plays their lawyer.
While the marriage between the Roses at first seems idyllic, cracks appear quickly and constantly throughout the film's runtime. The story turns into an unsettling war of a divorce that, while often hilarious, is also palpable in its cruelty, making the film a challenge for some to watch.
Still, based on a novel by Warren Adler, The War of the Roses is full of great substance, and is an entertaining, even if sometimes difficult, watch. The story was also recently remade in another strong film, 2025's The Roses.
A Separation
Global cinema has given excellent insight into how marriages and divorces function throughout the world, and A Separation is one of the strongest examples of this. Asghar Farhadi's 2011 Iranian drama was a huge achievement, and even won the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.
Built around family complications, the film sees Simin looking to leave Iran with their daughter in order to find a better life. Meanwhile, her husband wishes to stay, due to his father's medical needs. The film escalates, examining the complexities of family duties, immigration, and Iran's legal system.
A thoughtful film with a great deal to say, A Separation gives a fantastic look at relationships in Iran, and how even the most well-meaning characters can have their intentions corrupted by the machinations of separation.
Possession (1981)
The 1981 horror film Possession, which is itself being remade for 2027, is a fantastic entry in the genre. Sam Neill plays Mark, a spy who returns home only to learn that his wife, Anna, is sleeping with someone else and wishes to file for divorce.
The film leans into the texture of its Cold War setting, and highlights great feelings of alienation.
As a horror film, Possession goes to some interesting places. Director Andrzej Żuławski uses supernatural horrors in the film to express the psychological destruction of a relationship falling apart, as Mark discovers a terrifying creature with some shocking implications for the film's story.
Terrifying and raw all at once, the human story behind Possession is what makes it so strong. A horror with fantastic depth, it is an essential genre watch in the canon of films about divorce.
Kramer Vs. Kramer
Movies about heartbreak are necessarily difficult, but they can also show growth in unexpected ways. The 1979 legal drama Kramer vs. Kramer is a fantastic example of this, built around the separation and eventual divorce of Ted and Joanna Kramer, played by Dustin Hoffman and Meryl Streep, respectively.
The film took an unprecedented look at gender roles, uniquely examining a father's place in caring for his child. When Joanna suddenly decides to leave her marriage, it is up to Ted to stay behind and commit himself to his relationship with his son, giving the child a loving home throughout devastating emotional turmoil.
Giving eyes into a contentious battle for custody, the film shows the ruthlessness that a divorce can bring out between two people who love one another. However, its focus on family helps to make Kramer vs. Kramer one of the best movies of the 1970s.
Stepmom
While not a perfect movie, there is much to enjoy in the 1998 film Stepmom. The film takes a complex eye to changing ideas of what makes up a family, telling the story of two women navigating their place in looking after a pair of children.
Susan Sarandon plays Jackie Harrison, a divorced mother who has been diagnosed with a terminal illness. To complicate her life further, as she attempts to co-parent her two children along with her ex-husband, Luke's new girlfriend, Julia Roberts' Isabel, moves in and creates a whole new dynamic within the family.
Balancing ideas about parenting and caretaking, the film takes some surprisingly thoughtful turns, even if it occasionally leans a little saccharine. With great performances at its core, it remains an excellent film.
Is This Thing On?
An unusually interesting look at processing the dissolution of a relationship, Bradley Cooper's Is This Thing On? centers on the dynamics between Will Arnett's Alex and Laura Dern's Tess. Married long ago, and now in their forties, each reckons with the fact that they have given up things for their dynamic and to raise children together.
Their split is not bitter, and the two move on to a new phase in each of their lives. Tess dedicates herself to coaching, while Alex turns to the world of stand-up comedy, which helps to process how he really feels about his life and his relationships.
A complex look at marriage and divorce, Is This Thing On? brings a unique lens to a complicated subject, and creates something that feels both honest and genuinely thoughtful.
Crazy, Stupid, Love
Crazy, Stupid, Love is a compelling and smart romantic comedy that is full of fantastic stars. Steve Carell plays the central role of Cal, a middle-aged man whose wife asks him for a divorce. Unprepared for these events, he is helped by Jacob, an attractive and charismatic younger man played by Ryan Gosling, to meet women.
Of course, things quickly get messy. Jacob meets and falls in love with Emma Stone's Hannah, who turns out to be Cal's daughter. The dynamics become confused, and real questions about relationships, lifestyles, and suitability for partnership come to the fore.
Crazy, Stupid, Love confronts some real concerns about attraction, relationships, and showing up for one another. The script is genuinely funny and charming, and the characters are excellent.
Mrs. Doubtfire
One of the strongest movies that defined Robin Williams' career, Mrs. Doubtfire is a fantastic comedy that hinges on a stunningly charismatic performance. The film centers around Daniel Hillard, who, after his wife files for divorce, finds himself losing custody of his children until he is able to find and maintain a steady job.
In response, Daniel launches a scheme that is silly, but full of heart. He disguises himself as Euphegenia Doubtfire and takes on a job in his family home as a nanny. This affords him the opportunity to maintain a relationship with his children while also working a second job at a TV station.
The premise is a bit outsized and silly, but the execution is what makes the movie so strong. Williams balances comedy and real emotion as both Daniel and Mrs. Doubtfire, allowing the heavy subject matter of the film to be even more effective.
The Awful Truth (1937)
A silly, screwball comedy from the 1930s, The Awful Truth is an amusing story about a couple who enter into proceedings for divorce. There is a 90-day waiting period to process it, and in the meantime, each of the two pursues other romantic connections.
Still, neither seems to be able to let go of the other, and is unwilling to see them with anyone else. Cary Grant's Jerry and Irene Dunne's Lucy sabotage each other's new relationships at every turn, resulting in some excellent humor.
The stars had great chemistry, and the film relied heavily on their shared charisma as well as improvisation. It remains one of the best romantic comedies in the history of classic Hollywood.

item.title: [TODAY.com] Gwyneth Paltrow Reveals Story Behind Her ‘Conscious Uncoupling’ With Chris Martin

item.content:encoded:
When Gwyneth Paltrow and Chris Martin used the term “conscious uncoupling” to describe their separation in 2014, the phrase ended up going viral at the time, taking the internet by storm.
And now, we finally have its backstory.
Paltrow, 53, opened up about the term during a recent episode of podcast “Friends Keep Secrets.” It turns out, her introduction to the phrase came from a therapist that she and Martin had at the time.
“Chris and I had this therapist that was really brilliant, and he sort of introduced us to the concept,” Paltrow told hosts Benny Blanco, Lil Dicky and his wife Kristin Batalucco during the Sept. 8 episode. “We just made a commitment to really put the kids first, and so what that meant was to stay a family, even though we weren’t a couple.”
Paltrow — who is currently married to writer and director Brad Falchuk, 55 — shares two children with Martin, 49. The two announced the news of the divorce through a statement on her Goop website.
“We are parents first and foremost, to two incredibly wonderful children and we ask for their and our space and privacy to be respected at this difficult time,” Paltrow and Martin wrote in the statement. “We have always conducted our relationship privately, and we hope that as we consciously uncouple and coparent, we will be able to continue in the same manner.”
Paltrow told the podcast that when she and Martin decided to get divorced, she turned to friends who came from divorced households for guidance.
“I said, ‘Tell me, what was the worst thing? What do you feel you have scars from to this day?’” Paltrow recounted. “They said the worst part was ... ‘My dad used to drop me off at the end of the driveway.’ ‘It was so tense at my birthday parties.’ ‘They never ate dinner in the same room until my college graduation, and it caused me so much pain.’”
She added that she and Martin sought to “circumvent all of that awful stuff.” Paltrow also shared one particular trying moment during the divorce in which she had to put the conscious uncoupling philosophy to work. She explained that when the family moved to Los Angeles early on in the separation, they continued to have brunch together every Sunday. One particular brunch date proved difficult.
“Chris and I were upset with each other about something – I can’t even remember what it is — and I was like, ‘This might go really off the rails,’” she recalled. “It was getting tense, and we looked at each other. We went outside on the front porch, and we’re like, ‘Let’s just not.’”
She said that the two ended up embracing.
“We just hugged,” she said. “We like fist-bumped and then we went to brunch.”
Paltrow, to be clear, did not invent the term “conscious uncoupling.” The tactic, believed to be coined by late marriage and family therapist Katherine Woodward Thomas, has long existed with therapists and counselors encouraging the mindset as part of the final stage of marriage counseling after a decision to divorce is made.
Life coach Jeanne Byrd Romero previously told TODAY.com that conscious uncoupling is a method that can help the parties heal.
“It’s really a way of moving out of blame and shame so people can transform the experience into healing and peace,” Romero said. “It can be done with just one of the partners are the couple.”

item.content:encoded:
Gwyneth Paltrow unveils why she called Chris Martin divorce 'conscious uncoupling'
Gwyneth Paltrow and Chris Martin welcomed two kids, daughter Apple and son Moses
Gwyneth Paltrow and Chris Martin planned to "stay a family" after they parted ways.
The actress and the Coldplay frontman caused a stir back in 2014 when they first described their divorce as "conscious uncoupling.”
Now, the Marty Supreme star has described why they used the term and how they wanted to separate as smoothly as possible for their kids, daughter Apple Martin and son Moses.
“We really sat down and thought, like, is there a way that we could do this?" she said on the Friends Keep Secrets podcast.
She continued, “I talked to all my friends who came from a divorced household and I said, ‘Tell me what was the worst thing? Like, what do you feel you have scars from to this day?’”
Gwyneth admitted she was shocked to discover the problem was not the divorce but the challenges kids face growing up amid friction between parents.
The mom of two noted, “They said the worst part was like my parents, you know, my dad used to drop me off at the end of the driveway. Like it was so tense at my birthday parties, you know, they never ate dinner in the same room until my college graduation, and it caused me so much pain. So I was like, how could we not do that?”
So Gwyneth wanted her kids to grow up in a situation where “you’re all having dinner at the same table” no matter what.
She recalled, “So Chris and I had this therapist that was really brilliant, and he sort of introduced us to the concept and we just made a commitment to really put the kids first and so what that meant was to stay a family even though we weren’t a couple."
It is pertinent to mention that Gwyneth is now married to Brad Falchuk

item.content:encoded:
Frankie Muniz isn’t racing away from his struggles.
The Malcolm in the Middle actor got candid about what he’s been going through over the last six weeks, admitting his life has felt like “a nightmare I’m praying to wake up from.”
“Everything felt heavy, unclear, and like it was falling apart at the same time,” Muniz posted on X Sept. 18. “I wouldn’t wish this season on anyone.”
The admission comes over two months after he and wife Paige Price—with whom he shares 5-year-old son Mauz Mosley Muniz—announced their divorce after six years of marriage.
Still, there is a silver lining for the 40-year-old, as he explained, “The unexpected gift in the middle of it is that I’ve had nowhere to hide. I’ve had time to sit with myself, do real self-reflection, and finally see the areas of my life that need work if I want to become a better version of me. Not the polished version I show the world...the actual one.”
Muniz said he recently read that "sometimes hitting rock bottom is the thing that wakes you up" and becomes a catalyst to force “the changes you needed to make all along so you can live the best life possible.”
And that idea stayed with the race car driver, who imagined in five years time he will “look back at this exact low point and feel grateful for it,” especially because getting to a better place in his life necessitated going through the difficulty.
“This isn’t the end of the story. It’s the part where I start doing the work...the uncomfortable, unglamorous, necessary work. I’m choosing to treat this season as the foundation, not the finish line,” Muniz wrote. “If you’re in a low place right now too, you’re not broken. You’re being rebuilt. Let's keep going!”
In recent weeks, Muniz has been open about the difficult time he’s been facing, posting on X Aug. 26, “Am I naive to say that I didn't know that having a broken heart actually meant your heart physically aches. I'd rather break my back again.”
On Sept. 1 he wrote, “Struggling,” and a few days later on Sept. 6 shared two photos of himself as a child, captioning the pictures, “Sometimes I wish I could go back to this.”
For more stars who have been candid about their own struggles, keep reading.
